correctness.rationale: The primary theorem supplies the necessary branch shape and equation. Rearrangement gives the exact product identity \((b+2)(3t-2-a)=3(2t-1)\), so setting \(d=b+2\) yields the displayed divisor parametrization. Conversely every nontrivial divisor gives nonnegative integer exponents, and after imposing \(a,b\ge2\) exactly the divisors \(1\) and \(3\) are excluded; for \(d>3\) and \(t\ge2\), the lower bound on \(a\) is automatic. Direct computation of \(\varphi(3^aP_t^b)=4\cdot3^{a+t-1}P_t^{b-1}\) makes \(\tau(\varphi(n))=3(a+t)b\), while \(\tau(n^2)=(2a+1)(2b+1)\), so the exponent equation is also sufficient. An independent brute-force check through \(t=20\) matched every divisor solution; it corroborates rather than replaces the algebraic proof.

originality.rationale: The 2023 primary paper proves only the necessary reduction to \(3^a(2\cdot3^t+1)^b\) with the exponent equation \(ab+2a+2b+1=3bt\), and its conclusion explicitly lists solving the resulting Diophantine system as further work. The audited factorization solves that open subproblem completely and then verifies the converse to obtain an iff branch classification. Resultary found the audited record as the direct exact match and no earlier parametrization.

final_claim: In the odd two-prime branch \(n=q_1^a q_2^b\) with \(a,b\ge2\), \(\tau(n^2)=\tau(\varphi(n))\) holds exactly for \(q_1=3\), \(q_2=2\cdot3^t+1\) prime, and divisors \(d>3\) of \(3(2t-1)\) with \(b=d-2\) and \(a=3t-2-3(2t-1)/d\); hence each admissible \(t\) contributes exactly \(\tau(3(2t-1))-2\) solutions.
